issues.legal_issue: A partisan eyewitness’s testimony can sustain a criminal conviction without independent corroboration when the witness’s presence and account are credible and the evidence is consistent with the surrounding circumstances and medical evidence.
material_facts: The eyewitness was associated with the deceased’s side, but his presence at the scene was not in doubt.
He intervened in the assault, was injured, and had a close opportunity to observe the attackers.
He attributed the fatal injuries to only two attackers and gave his account with restraint.
The medical evidence was consistent with the account of the injuries caused by sharp-pointed weapons.
issues.conclusion: The eyewitness’s testimony, supported by the medical evidence, was sufficient to sustain the murder convictions.
issues.legal_principle: There is no hard and fast rule that a partisan witness’s evidence cannot be acted upon without corroboration. If the witness’s presence is reliable and the testimony is consistent with the surrounding circumstances and probabilities, and appears true, it can form the basis of conviction; medical evidence may provide assurance. The Court relied on no earlier cases or specific statutory provision for this evidentiary principle.

rule.if: criminal_conviction_appeal and partisan_eyewitness and eyewitness_presence_reliable and restrained_specific_testimony and medical_evidence_consistent

predicates.criminal_conviction_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal challenging a criminal conviction.
predicates.partisan_eyewitness: An eyewitness is associated with one side of the dispute.
predicates.eyewitness_presence_reliable: The eyewitness’s presence at the scene and opportunity to observe are supported by the circumstances.
predicates.restrained_specific_testimony: The eyewitness gives a restrained account that identifies particular acts rather than indiscriminately accusing everyone present.
predicates.medical_evidence_consistent: Medical evidence is consistent with material parts of the eyewitness’s account.

issues.definition: When a criminal conviction is appealed and a partisan eyewitness was reliably present, gives a restrained and specific account, and is supported by consistent medical evidence, the conviction may rest on that testimony.

issues.legal_issue: A general account in an initial report does not make later, more specific eyewitness testimony a material change when the initial informant observed the incident from a distance and another witness had a better opportunity to observe it closely.
material_facts: The initial report stated generally that the accused surrounded the deceased and used their weapons, without specifying which accused injured which person.
The informant was the injured eyewitness’s son and may have observed the incident from a distance.
The injured eyewitness had intervened and was close to the victims, allowing him to identify the particular attackers.
issues.conclusion: The difference between the general account in the initial report and the later specific testimony did not amount to a material change in the prosecution case.
issues.legal_principle: Witnesses observing a crowded assault from varying distances cannot be expected to give more than a general account. A witness who intervenes and observes the incident at close range may naturally provide particulars omitted from the initial report. The Court relied on no earlier cases or specific statutory provision for this conclusion.

rule.if: criminal_conviction_appeal and initial_report_general and initial_informant_observed_from_distance and later_witness_observed_at_close_range

predicates.criminal_conviction_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal challenging a criminal conviction.
predicates.initial_report_general: The initial report describes the incident generally without assigning specific acts to individual participants.
predicates.initial_informant_observed_from_distance: The person who made the initial report observed the incident from a distance or otherwise lacked a close view.
predicates.later_witness_observed_at_close_range: A later witness had a close opportunity to observe the incident and identify individual acts.

issues.definition: When an initial report is general because its informant observed from a distance, more specific testimony from a witness with a close view is not, for that reason alone, materially inconsistent.

issues.legal_issue: The acquittal of some accused does not by itself invalidate testimony against other accused when the witness’s account of the latter’s acts is independently supported.
material_facts: The eyewitness said that some of the other accused instigated the attackers.
The High Court acquitted those accused as a matter of abundant caution.
Medical evidence corroborated the account of the appellants’ acts but did not provide the same corroboration against the acquitted accused.
issues.conclusion: The acquittal of the other accused did not require rejection of the eyewitness’s testimony against the appellants.
issues.legal_principle: An acquittal of some persons implicated by a witness does not necessarily establish that the witness falsely implicated the remaining accused. The evidentiary basis may differ between accused, including where medical evidence corroborates the account against some but not others. The Court relied on no earlier cases or specific statutory provision for this conclusion.

predicates.criminal_conviction_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal challenging a criminal conviction.
predicates.witness_implicated_multiple_accused: A witness attributes acts or participation to more than one accused.
predicates.corroboration_differs_between_accused: Evidence corroborates the witness’s account against some accused more strongly than against others.

issues.definition: When a witness implicates multiple accused but the supporting evidence differs between them, acquittal of some does not by itself invalidate the testimony against the others.

issues.legal_issue: A conviction for attempted murder is not sustained where the accused’s responsibility for the grievous injury is not established, although the evidence establishes that the accused caused simple hurt with a sharp weapon.
material_facts: The accused was found to have inflicted one of two spear injuries on the victim.
One injury was grievous and located on the chest, while the other was simple and located on the thigh.
The eyewitness did not identify which injury the accused inflicted.
issues.conclusion: The attempted-murder conviction was altered to a conviction for causing simple hurt with a sharp weapon, and the sentence was reduced.
issues.legal_principle: The Court distinguished the offence under Section 307 of the Penal Code from causing hurt with a sharp weapon under Section 324. Because the evidence did not identify the grievous injury as the one inflicted by the accused, the Court, as a matter of caution, convicted him only for causing simple hurt with a sharp weapon. No earlier case was cited.

rule.if: criminal_conviction_appeal and accused_caused_one_of_multiple_injuries and injuries_differ_in_severity and grievous_injury_not_attributed_to_accused and sharp_weapon_used

predicates.criminal_conviction_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal challenging a criminal conviction.
predicates.accused_caused_one_of_multiple_injuries: The evidence establishes that the accused inflicted one injury among multiple injuries suffered by the victim.
predicates.injuries_differ_in_severity: The victim suffered injuries that differ in severity, including a grievous injury and a simple injury.
predicates.grievous_injury_not_attributed_to_accuse: The evidence does not establish that the accused inflicted the grievous injury.
predicates.sharp_weapon_used: The injury attributed to the accused was inflicted with a sharp weapon.

issues.definition: When an accused caused one of several injuries but the evidence does not attribute the grievous injury to that accused, proof that a sharp weapon was used supports conviction only for simple hurt with that weapon.
